Consult Summary:
- 34-year-old female, 4 weeks post-cesarean section, presented with acute onset shortness of breath and recent cough, advised urgent hospital assessment for possible post-partum clot.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute onset shortness of breath while seated, started approximately one hour prior to consult.
- Timeline:
    - Cough began yesterday.
    - Shortness of breath began within the last hour.
    - No prior episodes of shortness of breath.
    - C-section performed four weeks ago.
- Associated symptoms:
    - Palpitations (“heart is really going”).
    - No chest pain, but chest feels sore on deep breath (also notes general tenderness from C-section scar).
    - No sputum production with cough.
    - No current or recent cold/flu (last episode “a few months ago”).
    - No symptoms in baby.
- No noted exacerbating or relieving factors.
- No mention of fevers, leg swelling, or other systems review findings.

Past Medical History:
- Cesarean section four weeks ago.
- No mention of other chronic medical conditions.
- No current medications, but was taking Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented) for pain post-operatively; last taken approximately one week ago.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen (reaction type unknown).

Social History:
- Lives at home with partner (currently at work).
- Has a newborn at home; currently sole caregiver.
- No mention of smoking, alcohol, or recreational drug use.
- No financial or other social issues discussed.

Family History:
- Mother has history of leg clots (deep vein thrombosis).

Physical Examination:
- Heart rate measurement by patient (palpated radial pulse): 30 beats over unspecified period (timing of pulse count not specified, limiting interpretation).
- No documented vitals.
- No other examination findings.

Investigations:
- None performed in this setting.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute onset shortness of breath in a post-cesarean patient (4 weeks postpartum) with family history of clots.
  - Clinical impression: Possible pulmonary embolism or other post-partum thromboembolic event.
  - Plan:
    - Advise urgent hospital assessment for further evaluation and management.
    - Instruct patient not to take further Codeine at this time.
    - Advise to bring baby and prepare for potentially rapid hospital visit.
    - Discussed risks of clots and need for hospital-based investigation and treatment if required.
- General plan:
    - Provided options for ambulance transport versus self-transport; patient elected self-transport.

Quality checks:

● Missing clinically expected elements:
    - No documented full medication reconciliation outside Codeine.
    - No detailed allergy reaction information for Ibuprofen.
    - No reported vital signs beyond self-palpated pulse count.
    - No review of systems beyond respiratory and cardiac.
    - No detailed physical exam (e.g., leg swelling, respiratory exam).
    - Smoking and alcohol history not discussed.
    - No documentation of past medical/surgical history beyond recent C-section.

● Conflicts noted:
    - Patient’s date of birth cited as both 1980 and 1983 (conflict noted).

● Transcript quality:
    - Transcript provides all essential information but some details (e.g., timing of pulse measurement) are imprecise. No significant audio quality concerns.
